title: Normalized tensor operations for a given pointwise comparison
statement: For every family c of Comparison records over the bases P [def-per-lisse-completed-system-data], tensor pullback and finite coefficient extension give TensorOperations c. This consists of Operation a for each scheme/coefficient arrow a, integral and rational tensor identity and composition isomorphisms normalized by the actual adjunction units, and the counit-mate equation relating each reconstruction to reduction. It asserts none of the identity/composition comparison equations on the etale or raw rational categories.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and (4), with Corollary 5.1.5 for classical finite local systems; the comparison maps are reduction, inverse limit and localization. Their pullback and coefficient-extension compatibilities use these same maps. Etale-local existence of lattices is cited separately as an existing DAG node.

proof.text:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism between schemes satisfying the statement's hypotheses. Use the underlying sheaf inverse image $f^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Form $f^*N=B_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}B_X}f^{-1}N$ with the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the coefficient map $f^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ induced by the residue projections. The action on $f^{-1}N$ is the inverse image of the action on $N$, using finite-product preservation. The inverse-image tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] identifies
$$(f^*N)/\varpi^n\cong f_n^*(N/\varpi^nN).$$
On a pure tensor it sends the class of $b\otimes x$ to $\bar b\otimes\bar x$; the inverse sends $\bar b\otimes\bar x$ to that class, with lift independence following from the quotient relation. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], the finite etale and pro-etale pullbacks in this formula agree. For a tower $(N_n)$ the resulting maps to $\nu_Y^*f_{n,\mathrm{et}}^*N_n$ are compatible with its transitions, hence give
$$f^*(\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*N_n)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n\nu_Y^*f_{n,\mathrm{et}}^*N_n.$$
This map is an isomorphism on a pulled-back trivializing covering: a compatible basis furnished by step 4 identifies it with $B_Y^r\to\varprojlim_n(A_n)_Y^r$, the coefficient-limit isomorphism coordinate by coordinate. Thus it is an isomorphism globally. This proves the inverse-limit compatibility without claiming that inverse image preserves arbitrary inverse limits.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1): pullback naturality of the residue maps and inverse-limit reconstruction

proof.text:
For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ write $A'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, choose $\varpi'$, and let $e$ be its ramification index. The scalar-extension tower of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](3) has $m$-th term $N_{n(m)}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n(m)}}A'/\varpi'^m$, with $n(m)=\lceil m/e\rceil$; the coefficient map exists because $\varpi^{n(m)}\in\varpi'^mA'$. Put $B'_X=\varprojlim_m(A'/\varpi'^m)_X$. With the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], residue projections define a map
$$B'_X\otimes_{B_X}N\longrightarrow\varprojlim_m\nu_X^*\bigl(N_{n(m)}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n(m)}}A'/\varpi'^m\bigr),$$
whose $m$-th component sends $b'\otimes x$ to $\bar b'\otimes\bar x$. The finite comparison in step 3 justifies the finite-level tensor identification. The formula commutes with transitions: both composites reduce $b'$ and $x$ to the smaller quotient. On a compatible trivializing basis for $N$ from step 4 the map is $B'_X{}^r\to\varprojlim_m(A'/\varpi'^m)_X^r$, an isomorphism by the coefficient-limit identification of step 1 applied to $E'$. Thus scalar extension corresponds to precisely this tower, and reduction and reconstruction commute with it. No flatness of a map between the finite quotient rings is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and Lemma 6.8.2: finite coefficient-extension comparisons, with the ramified reindexing of Weil II (1.1.1)

proof.text: Finally scalar localization is the sheaf tensor $N[1/\varpi]=E_X\otimes_{B_X}N$. The pullback and finite-extension comparisons extend to these rational realizations by the same balanced-tensor maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On local fractions the pullback comparison sends $b\otimes(x/\varpi^k)$ to $(b\otimes x)/\varpi^k$; extension to $E'$ sends $a'\otimes(x/\varpi^k)$ to $a'\otimes x$ divided by the image of $\varpi^k$. This image is invertible in $E'$ even when the extension is ramified. These maps are isomorphisms on a pulled-back or extended finite-free basis and hence globally. On a raw rational morphism $\varpi^{-k}h$, the formula in step 6 is carried to $\varpi^{-k}f^*h$, or to the image of $\varpi^{-k}$ times the extended $h$, respectively, exactly the rational scalar-extension rule of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](2),(3). The equations in step 9 persist on fractions, since both routes give the same coefficient product and the same integral vector. Thus rational realization commutes with the specified pullbacks and finite coefficient extensions, with the required identity and composition equations. For $X=\varnothing$ all module sheaves are zero and all formulas reduce to the unique map.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(4): localization of the canonical integral comparisons

proof.text: Choose the ambient tensor identity and composition isomorphisms on generators. Verify their unit equations on 1 tensor x and c tensor (b tensor x). The reconstruction comparison is the counit mate of reduction: after quotient projection and the adjunction unit both sides are the same finite tensor map. Quotient universality and limit projection uniqueness imply the mate equation. No etale or raw identity/composition isomorphisms are chosen here.
